question: Can isolation reduce investment when autonomous selfing capacity cannot evolve?
exposure: Sustained near distance0 and far distance3, identical frozen visitor histories to previous extension
founders: Same original48 founders for matching and investment, with both assurance alleles set to0.5 in BOTH modes. Retain matched initial states; this is a new intervention cohort, not the original varying-assurance founders.
fixed: Config assurance_mode=fixed and fixed_assurance=0.5. Disable mutation only at assurance locus; matching/investment inheritance and mutation unchanged.
evolving: Config assurance_mode=evolving; all loci may mutate. Assurance evolution therefore requires mutation because founder assurance variance is zero.
negative_control: At mutation0 both modes must have exactly identical trajectories under matched history/replicate because assurance remains0.5 in either mode.
analysis: Paired history-level isolation effects within each mode, then difference in isolation effects between modes.5000 history bootstrap draws;95% descriptive intervals. Report persistence and pair eligibility separately. Complete full declared campaign before biological readout; no outcome-based stopping.
predictions: Investment can decline under fixed capacity if reduced visitor returns favour reduced investment cost
Allowing capacity evolution may modify isolation effects, with no imposed direction
limits: One intermediate fixed capacity only; not a universal mediation fraction. Capacity fixed does not mean realized selfing fixed. Both cohorts have altered founder assurance variance relative to main experiment. Timing and capacity cost remain a joint setting contrast. Mutation0 is a structural negative control, not evidence that assurance evolution is biologically absent.
